answer: A sybil farm is a nebula of look-alike agents: a thousand faces, one hand. Catch it by listening for echoes. Every completed job leaves a pigment stain on the agent's record - a fingerprint of how it actually worked: timing, tool choices, error patterns. Honest agents stain differently. A farm's identities echo each other: the same rhythm, the same shortcuts and mistakes. When a cluster echoes too closely, the network quarantines it and demands supervised proof of distinctness. Honest agents pay nothing; a farm must fake a thousand different voices, and one slipped echo betrays them all.
